layman_headline: Market fear is at extreme levels — sitting on the sidelines until the picture clears up.
layman_explanation: The crypto market is deep in 'Extreme Fear' territory at 25/100, and the mood has been getting worse all week. Bitcoin is holding around $64K but a prominent analyst just called for a drop to $43.5K. The swing trade candidates today are either low-quality setups (missing key technical data like RSI and chart patterns) or already overextended. LDO dropped 25% in a week which looks like a potential bounce play, but without reliable RSI confirmation, funding rate data, or chart patterns on most candidates, the risk of catching a falling knife is too high.
layman_action: Do nothing right now. Keep your cash ready. If Fear & Greed drops further or Bitcoin breaks below $63K, there may be better entries ahead. If the market stabilizes and fear starts to ease, that's the safer time to deploy capital.
expert_reasoning: Applying validated Rule #3: Fear & Greed at 25 means the short-term outlook is genuinely ambiguous, so HOLD is the safest call. Rule #7 notes that at extreme fear readings like this, BTC tends to drift down another 1-4% over the following week, though this is based on limited observations. Of the swing candidates, LDO has the best risk/reward ratio (2.91x) and a sharp mean-reversion setup after -24.9% in 7 days, but RSI at 43 is not yet in the oversold zone (sub-30) that our signal credibility data shows as reliable (71% win rate). BTW is overbought at RSI 69 with a terrible 0.29x risk/reward — a clear avoid. ETHFI, AAVE, MON, and UB all lack RSI data, chart analysis, and funding rates, meaning we'd be flying blind. The macro backdrop is mixed: institutional adoption news (BNY staking, Wells Fargo tokenization) is constructive longer-term, but the Terpin $43.5K call and HYPE ETF outflows signal near-term risk-off behavior.

context_banner: Extreme Fear dominates the market — capital preservation takes priority over chasing setups with incomplete data.
